newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The rand ended weaker on Thursday after late offshore dollar demand thwarted what dealers said were attempts by the Reserve Bank to cap the currency at the 4.48 level.
At the local 1400 GMT close, the rand was pegged at 4.4815/4845 against the dollar from 4.4710/4740 on Wednesday.
The currency initially staged an assault on the 4.46 level on the back of exporter dollar selling.

It's strength in the morning was also put down to comments by Finance Minister Trevor Manuel that the government would achieve its four percent 1997/98 budget deficit target without using proceeds from privatisation.
"There was no direct link between Manuel's comments and the rand's strengthening, but the comments were positive," a trader said.
In the afternoon session importer demand surfaced, nudging the rand just over the 4.48 level.
"We saw a fair amount of importer demand late in the afternoon which pushed it towards 4.48 and above," a trader said, adding that there had been two fairly large orders of $45 and $30 million each.
At the 4.48 level, dealers said the currency suddenly looked well offered, prompting speculation that the central bank had supported the currency by selling dollars through the smaller banks.
"From price action that happened around the figure (4.48), it would indicate it was (the central bank)," a trader said.

Shortly before the close, dealers also reported dollar demand out of New York which pushed the rand to its weakest level on the day of 4.4860 bid. The demand appeared to be linked to profit-taking, a trader said.
Against the crosses, the rand was relatively subdued. It was last quoted at 7.2128/2230 against sterling from 7.2240/2333 overnight and at 0.3754/3758 marks from 0.3770/3774 previously.
